What PMs, superintendents, managers and removal mean

A project manager (PM) has their own login to the company account: they see and do what the company account does on every job, and get the alerts of the jobs they are assigned to. A superintendent is a PM with that title: exactly the same access. Each PM or superintendent is a paid seat. A PM can’t change billing or ownership, and can’t change or remove the owner or another PM. Managers can read reports and dashboards and edit plans. Only the owner can make or remove PMs, superintendents and managers. Removing someone takes away their access to company screens. Everything they already filed (production, tickets, permits) stays the company’s, and their own records on their phone stay on their phone.
Alerts go to each job’s PMs and supers; with none, to every PM and super in the company.

Why Stats and Job Summary differ

Stats and Job Summary count differently, so their totals don’t have to match. Stats counts only runs locked with a pipe type, filtered here by time period, pipe type and jobsite. Job Summary counts every archived run under one job number, with or without a pipe type.
